A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GRADA. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and can be matched despite relocation, renumbering, and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack-defense experiments on NQ, MS-MARCO, and HotpotQA, including ablations, document-ranking analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations with Qwen2.5-14b-Instruct and the bge-small-en-v1.5 retriever.

M1.justification: The graph construction, D2DSIM/HRSIM scoring formulas, iterative ranking, uniform initialization, and top-n selection remain unchanged. The revised edge-weight range does not establish a new normalization step or other procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions report English question answering on NQ, MS-MARCO, and HotpotQA, with benign inputs and the same four attacks. The added generator and retriever are model configurations; no new dataset, task, or attack scenario is reported.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain HLATR, BGE-reranker, Keyword Aggregation, and the corresponding controls. Newly discussed TrustRAG and RAG-Forensics are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen2.5-14b-Instruct evaluations and a bge-small-en-v1.5 retriever experiment under benign inputs, PoisonedRAG, and PIA. Existing sample counts, retrieval settings, prompts, and ASR/EM definitions remain unchanged. Table 6 does not identify its dataset or generator.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.5 tests whether GRADA transfers to another retriever. Existing poisoning-count, initialization, similarity-function, ranking-distribution, and parameter analyses are retained; several move from the main text into Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds and use the same plus/minus uncertainty format. The added result rows follow that existing practice; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds Qwen2.5-14b results in Tables 10–14 and alternative-retriever results in Table 6. For example, Table 6 reports PoisonedRAG ASR/EM of 41.3/44.0 without defense and 5.3/62.3 with HRSIM. All matched pre-existing table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the stated edge-weight domain from positive reals to [0,1], a limited mathematical-definition revision. The scoring equations, ranking update, initialization mathematics, and complexity analysis are otherwise retained; no new proof is added.

C1.justification: The central graph-reranking contribution, hybrid scoring contribution, and claimed attack mitigation remain the same. Updating the abstract and introduction from five evaluated models to six reflects additional supporting evidence rather than a different core scientific claim.

C2.justification: Appendix C.5 adds an interpretation that the defense transfers across retrievers with limited utility loss. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations concerning multi-hop reasoning and a high proportion of poisoned documents remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F replaces the GitHub code-access pointer with an anonymous.4open.science repository pointer. Existing prompts, hardware, costs, and runtime disclosures remain. This establishes changed access information, not whether external availability improved or deteriorated.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhao et al. (2024) on third-party API attacks and discusses TrustRAG and RAG-Forensics as other interventions before generation. It also condenses the traditional web-spam discussion while retaining the existing cited works.

P1.justification: Several introductory, related-work, and explanatory paragraphs are edited. Most former Section 4.3 analyses move into Appendix C, while parameter sensitivity remains in the main discussion. The title and author block change, and acknowledgements are removed; the overall narrative remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the retriever-comparison table and expands five appendix tables with Qwen2.5-14b rows. Existing plots and the runtime table are relocated and renumbered, with corresponding page reflow. The figures retain their underlying visual content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's Contriever-only evaluation, v2 supplies a useful additional retriever check and another generator evaluation, modestly strengthening empirical support while retaining prior results. Related-work coverage also improves. The gain is limited by incomplete reporting of the dataset and generator behind the new retriever experiment in Table 6.
